breakfast.name: Sishwala (Sour Porridge)
instructions: Make porridge from mealie meal
Add fermented maize water for sourness
Cook until thick
Serve with sugar or milk

breakfast.name: Siphutfo (Sweet Potato Mash)
instructions: Boil sweet potatoes until tender
Mash with butter
Add sugar and cinnamon
breakfast.description: Mashed sweet potatoes — simple, filling breakfast.

breakfast.name: Sishwala (Fermented Porridge)
ingredients: Sour starter (fermented maize water from previous batch)
instructions: Mix maize meal with water and sour starter
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly — it should thicken and develop a tangy flavor
The fermentation gives it a sour, complex flavor different from regular porridge
Cook until thick and smooth — 15-20 min
Serve with sugar for breakfast or with meat/vegetables for a savory meal
The sour flavor is an acquired taste — but once you're used to it, plain porridge tastes flat
Every Eswatini household keeps a sour starter going — like a porridge sourdough
breakfast.description: Eswatini's fermented maize porridge — tangy, thick, and made with a continuously maintained sour starter (like a sourdough mother). The fermentation tradition and the 'acquired taste' challenge have gained attention in the global fermentation movement.

lunch.name: Sidvudvu (Pumpkin and Cornmeal)
instructions: Cook pumpkin, mash
Mix with mealie meal and water
Cook until thick, stirring constantly

lunch.name: Sishebo (Meat and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Brown beef
Add onion, tomatoes, pepper
Add curry powder and water
Add potatoes, simmer until tender

lunch.name: Umncweba (Dried Meat / Biltong)
instructions: Cut beef into strips along the grain — about 1cm thick
Splash with vinegar
Mix salt, coriander, pepper, sugar — rub into all surfaces
Hang strips in a cool, dry, ventilated place
Air-dry for 3-5 days depending on thickness and humidity
The meat should be dry on the outside, slightly moist inside — not jerky-hard
Slice thin against the grain to eat
This is Eswatini's version of the Southern African biltong/dried meat tradition
Every family has their spice blend — coriander is the signature
lunch.description: Eswatini's dried meat tradition — beef strips cured with coriander and salt, air-dried to perfection. Part of the broader Southern African biltong culture. The artisanal air-drying process and the 'better than jerky' comparison have made biltong and its regional variations viral globally.

dinner.name: Umncweba (Dried Meat)
instructions: Marinate beef strips in vinegar and spices
Hang to dry in sun and wind 3 days
When dry, eat as is or fry briefly

dinner.name: Chicken Stew with Emahewu
instructions: Brown chicken pieces
Add vegetables and water
Simmer 30 min until done
Serve with pap or rice

dinner.name: Incwancwa (Sour Porridge with Stew)
ingredients: Sour porridge: fermented maize meal (sishwala), water
Stew: beef or chicken, tomatoes, onion, garlic
instructions: Make sishwala (sour porridge) — thick and tangy
Make stew: brown meat, add onion, tomatoes, garlic
Simmer until meat is tender
Add greens and optional peanut butter — it enriches the sauce
Season with salt and chili
Serve porridge in a communal bowl with stew ladled over
This combination — sour starch with rich, meaty stew — is the bedrock of Swazi cuisine
The tanginess of the porridge cuts through the richness of the stew perfectly
dinner.description: The foundation of Swazi cuisine — tangy fermented porridge paired with a rich meat-and-vegetable stew. The sour-rich contrast is the principle behind Eswatini's food philosophy. Communal eating from shared bowls is the tradition — food is social before it is personal.

snacks.name: Mealie Bread
instructions: Mix dry ingredients
Add wet ingredients
Pour into loaf pan
Bake at 180°C 45 min

snacks.name: Magwinya (Fried Fat Cakes)
ingredients: Filling: mince, atchar (pickled mango), or polony
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt
Add warm water gradually — dough should be soft and slightly sticky
Knead briefly, cover, let rise 1 hour until doubled
Heat oil to 170°C
Pull off golf-ball-sized pieces, drop into oil
Fry until puffed and deep golden — about 4 min, turning once
Drain briefly
Split and fill with mince, atchar, or eat plain with tea
Every taxi rank, market, and school gate in Eswatini has a magwinya vendor
The puff-up moment and the filling choices are endlessly viral across Southern Africa
snacks.description: Southern Africa's beloved fried bread — pillowy dough balls that puff up dramatically when fried. Found at every market, taxi rank, and school gate in Eswatini. The puffing moment and the split-and-fill technique are viral across the region — the Southern African answer to beignets.

desserts.name: Tinkhobe (Boiled Corn)
instructions: Soak corn overnight
Boil until tender, about 1 hour
Toss with ground peanuts and sugar
desserts.description: Boiled corn with peanuts — a sweet traditional snack-dessert.

desserts.name: Tinkhobe (Boiled Whole Corn Kernels)
instructions: Soak corn overnight
Boil corn and raw peanuts together in salted water for 1+ hour until tender
The peanuts soften and become creamy, the corn stays chewy
Season with sugar for a snack or salt for a side dish
Serve warm in bowls or cups
This is the simplest, most traditional Swazi snack — just corn and peanuts, boiled
Street vendors sell tinkhobe in paper cups — it's Eswatini's original comfort food
desserts.description: The simplest Swazi comfort food — dried corn and raw peanuts boiled together until the peanuts are creamy and the corn is chewy. Sold in paper cups at markets across Eswatini. The two-ingredient simplicity has gained attention as an example of how the best snacks need nothing but good ingredients and time.

drinks.name: Emahewu (Fermented Maize Drink)
instructions: Cook thin porridge, cool
Add malt
Let ferment 1-2 days
Serve cold

drinks.name: Umcombotsi (Traditional Beer)
instructions: Cook mealie meal porridge
Mix with sorghum malt
Ferment 3 days
Strain, serve at room temp
